newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PRESIDENT TO VISIT EASTERN EUROPEAN STATES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PRESIDENT TO VISIT EASTERN EUROPEAN STATES.

text.p: Bulgaria's new President Petar Stoynov will make a five-day trip to Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary from February 26, president's foreign policy secretary said on Monday.
"President Stoyanov will discuss bilateral relations in the framework of the new architecture of Europe and Bulgaria's will for full NATO membership," Vladimir Filipov told Reuters.

Stoyanov, who formerly took office on January 22 inheriting a severe economic and political crisis, is due to visit Poland on February 26-27, the Czech Republic on February 28-March 1 and Hungary on March 1-2.
On Monday Bulgaria's caretaker government adopted a declaration stating a desire for full NATO membership in a bid to clear the country's so far ambiguous policy on the issue.

The declaration, endorsed by Bulgarian president Petar Stoyanov, aims to qualify the Balkan country for membership nomination at a NATO summit in July, where the alliance will decide which new members to admit.

Reform-laggard Bulgaria has fallend behind top contenders in the race for memebership like Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, although like most ex-communist states, it takes part in NATO's Partnership for Peace initiative designed to foster cooperation between former Cold War foes.
